fields.name: field_0
fields.evidence: bg3.exe+0x191FE90 creates it as 4; bg3.exe+0x191E800 copies it verbatim from the first uint16 of the 4-byte per-entity request record (the hash map returned by bg3.exe+0x191EAE0). Same value range as the two states after it; not touched again in the functions read. Probe: always 4.

fields.name: State
fields.evidence: Created as 4 (bg3.exe+0x191FE90). bg3.exe+0x191E800 sets it from the second uint16 of the request record, with values 1,2,3,5,7 all turned into 7. bg3.exe+0x191E250 does [+4] = [+2]; [+2] = 7 for entities in the 'finished' set. bg3.exe+0x191EC10 reads it to pick which animation gameplay event to wait for (1 -> one event, 2 -> another, else a third). Probe: always 4.

fields.name: PreviousState
fields.evidence: bg3.exe+0x191E250: [+4] = [+2] right before [+2] is overwritten; bg3.exe+0x191E800 sets it together with +2 on creation. Probe: always 4.

open_questions: The three values are most likely of enum ls::model::game::item::animation::v0::EAnimationState (type name kept in the exe, bg3.exe+0x24BCC50); member names are not known - 4 is the idle default, 7 is the state everything collapses to after a transition, 1 and 2 wait for different animation events.
field_0: probably the state the item was asked to be in (requested / target state), not confirmed.

esv::item::animation::StateComponent: looks like the same struct. Same size 6; the savegame loader bg3.exe+0x25B68E0 builds it from three uint16 values written to +0, +2, +4, read from 0x18-byte records of ls::model::game::item::animation::v0::StateComponent. The server-side transition code (bg3.exe+0x35A1CE0) was not read, so the per-field meaning on the server is assumed, not checked; no section for it was found in probe-server.txt.
